Quick prep brief
Purpose of the meeting
The session is to kick off enhancements review and sizing for Sprint 2, specifically to check whether the team has enough information from the**“Must Have” tickets** and decide what can be reviewed/sized now versus what needs further clarification.
Review priority
[Re: [Review] Enhancements & Sizing](https://outlook.office365.com/owa/?ItemID=AAMkADAwMDY5M2RlLWQ4YTgtNDk0ZC05NjE0LWY5NDM4ODY2NjlmYwBGAAAAAADj6PLKElMiQqCITvdyZx6EBwBDVw5BF5KXS4J9nmOzC999AAAAAAEMAABDVw5BF5KXS4J9nmOzC999AAAe0PAnAAA%3d&exvsurl=1&viewmodel=ReadMessageItem&EntityRepresentationId=0acdfd83-0979-4cb1-a0eb-f17f8d59b5b0) says the meeting will review the https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-24?search_id=8285876f-f3cc-436f-9943-85be8017d2e1 in this order: Must Have’s not yet sized first, then Should Have’s, then Could Have’s.
What you should have ready
Come in with a sizing lens across these effort areas: BA effort, QA / SIT effort, Front End effort if any, Back End effort if any, and Architecture effort if any.
Given your frontend lead role on Zimmermann, I’d focus your prep on this simple mental model:

For each enhancement:
1. Is there any Front End impact?
2. Is the requirement clear enough to size?
3. Does it touch PWA Kit / React, Contentful, SFCC integration, checkout, account, PDP/PLP, or CMS-rendered areas?
4. Are there design/Figma dependencies?
5. Are there API/backend dependencies?
6. Is this a pure FE change, shared FE/BE change, or needs architecture input?
7. Can we size now, or do we need clarification?

Suggested stance for the meeting
You can frame your input like this:

For FE sizing, I’ll separate the tickets into:
- Clear enough to size now
- Needs design clarification
- Needs API/backend clarification
- Needs architecture decision
- No obvious FE impact
For anything touching UI, I’ll also call out whether the designs/design system are mature enough for us to size confidently, or whether we need assumptions documented before committing.

Questions worth asking
Use these if the discussion gets fuzzy:

* “Do we have enough acceptance criteria to size this, or should this go into clarification first?”
* “Is the expected UI already covered in Figma, or are we sizing based on assumptions?”
* “Is this enhancement purely frontend, or does it need backend/API support?”
* “Are we sizing implementation only, or also discovery/spike effort?”
* “Should we capture assumptions separately so the estimate doesn’t look more certain than it is?”
* “For Must Haves, do we need a minimum viable implementation for Sprint 2, or the full desired enhancement?”

Quick sizing template you can use live

Ticket:
Priority: Must / Should / Could
FE impact: Yes / No / Unknown
FE estimate:
BE dependency:
QA/SIT consideration:
Design dependency:
Architecture input needed: Yes / No
Clarifications required:
Sizing confidence: High / Medium / Low
Recommendation: Size now / Clarify first / Spike needed

People context
Required invitees include [Linsangan, Gideon R.](https://www.office.com/search?q=Linsangan%2c+Gideon+R.&EntityRepresentationId=a09dcabc-7f11-42fd-a47a-081c6e8e53ba), [Navarro, Marcel Angelo N.](https://www.office.com/search?q=Navarro%2c+Marcel+Angelo+N.&EntityRepresentationId=c6464783-afc3-4afa-825c-43fcb4a494af), [Chaloner, Isabel](https://www.office.com/search?q=Chaloner%2c+Isabel&EntityRepresentationId=00f4faa0-050a-4d4b-9880-6d9aa4b15b83), [Tsang, Jasmijn](https://www.office.com/search?q=Tsang%2c+Jasmijn&EntityRepresentationId=4c02c6a5-38bd-40a8-9378-35ffab98147a), [Ramachandran, Manikandan](https://www.office.com/search?q=Ramachandran%2c+Manikandan&EntityRepresentationId=ab53e6fe-d92b-4c59-bd50-14111a7f060d), and [Crisostomo, Victor T.](https://www.office.com/search?q=Crisostomo%2c+Victor+T.&EntityRepresentationId=c0b202e9-ee0d-435c-a543-8f5adfae31a7); optional invitees include [Lucy Fu](https://www.office.com/search?q=Lucy+Fu&EntityRepresentationId=6ede0339-cd04-4981-a1f3-6bf772481b29), [Rebecca Jourdan](https://www.office.com/search?q=Rebecca+Jourdan&EntityRepresentationId=18f5fd67-819f-4248-86db-b543d4364d7b), [Lavelle, Tim](https://www.office.com/search?q=Lavelle%2c+Tim&EntityRepresentationId=488f1fe0-33fb-4ab4-894e-9975ee7dca86), [Emma Kirwan](https://www.office.com/search?q=Emma+Kirwan&EntityRepresentationId=3f4610bd-c3ed-4f2f-b315-990a2231f15e), [Dani Rivett](https://www.office.com/search?q=Dani+Rivett&EntityRepresentationId=96ef42b2-8d8e-4bc2-938c-e036c26501f2), [Pagaduan, Jesse C.](https://www.office.com/search?q=Pagaduan%2c+Jesse+C.&EntityRepresentationId=15655688-6c9a-497e-97a1-d6500c999816), and [Cacalda, Hazel Marie](https://www.office.com/search?q=Cacalda%2c+Hazel+Marie&EntityRepresentationId=d1603ce6-a1dc-4b31-979b-29690c1c3ca5).
Your likely contribution
I’d go in ready to be the person who keeps the sizing grounded: call out where FE effort is straightforward, where UI/design maturity affects confidence, and where integration/backend clarification is needed before anyone treats an estimate as firm. That should help the team move through the Must Haves without overcommitting on under-specified tickets.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

  - `digital-sit.yml` (push/PR to `release/**`): four parallel jobs into `sit-gate` — `playwright-p0` (Chromium P0 suite), `bundle-size` (bundlewatch, main.js < 180 kB / vendor.js < 250 kB / main.css < 50 kB), `contract-tests` (placeholder; real MuleSoft OpenAPI assertion pending spec source), `lighthouse-ci` (Perf ≥ 80, A11y ≥ 90, Best Practices ≥ 90; requires LHCI server secrets)
- **`e2e-localhost` (qa.yml) is fixed and re-enabled, as of PR #35 (`bugfix/ci-e2e-test`, merged 2026-07-16).** Root cause of the "homepage smoke test fails in CI, logo never found" issue (open as of PR #30): `BasePage.js`'s old `dismissConsent()` wrapped both `waitFor()` and `.click()` in one `try/catch`, so a real click failure was silently swallowed as "no dialog appeared" — if a consent dialog genuinely appeared in CI (injected by something outside this repo's own source, e.g. GTM/MRT platform config — not by anything grep-visible in `overrides/`) and the click failed transiently, the `aria-modal` dialog stayed open and blocked the entire page's accessibility tree, exactly matching the symptom. Fixed by CodeRabbit-prompted review in PR #30 (separated `.click()` out of the `try/catch`) — but that fix was never actually exercised in CI until PR #35 re-enabled the job, confirmed via 4 consecutive clean CI passes. Along the way also: added an HTML reporter to `playwright.config.js` (every project except `p0` had been silently producing an empty `playwright-report/` — CI failures were undebuggable from artifacts alone); fixed a webpack-build-race (`wait-on` only confirms the port is open, not that the client bundle finished compiling — added a step polling `dev-server.log` for `webpack built client`); fixed the original missing-Commerce-API-env-vars bug (job now binds `environment: dev`, sources `COMMERCE_API_*` from `vars.*`, `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`'s `push <tier>` uploads a shared+tier merge so one environment binding is self-sufficient); switched the job gate from `always()` to `!cancelled()` so a superseded/cancelled run doesn't burn a 15-min runner slot.
- PR #30 (`feature/gh-qa-workflow`, merged) also: deleted the unfinished `SFCC-000_guest-checkout` placeholder (never had real Adyen payment interaction, self-described `EXAMPLE` in its own header) and its `testIgnore` mis-scoping (ran under `chromium`/`mobile-chrome` `retries:2` instead of the dedicated `p0` project's `retries:0`, costing ~12 of the ~14 min `e2e-localhost` runtime on every PR); added a homepage smoke test (new `homepage` E2E area + `SMOKE-` naming convention for Jira-less tests); fixed a `@typescript-eslint/no-var-requires` misconfiguration flagging `require()` in `e2e/`'s intentionally-CommonJS files; added `test-results/`/`playwright-report/` to `.gitignore`.
- **Proposed: tag-based environment promotion (GitFlow) — full spec on Confluence, implementation not yet started.** Full rationale, tag naming convention, worked commands, and open questions:
  [Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/335216656/Proposed+Tag-Based+Environment+Promotion+GitFlow)
  (Confluence, v5, child of the Branching Guide page). Summary: only `Dev` should be continuously tied to `develop`; every other tier should deploy a specific, immutable git tag (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`, cut via `npm version`) instead of a branch ref, so Test/SIT/UAT/Stage can each run independent testing cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. **Do not implement the AGENTS.md/governance pieces without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal.** Implementation checklist for a fresh session on a new branch (see the Confluence page for full detail on each item):
  - **Decided 2026-07-16** (see Confluence page's "Decisions made so far" table): release cadence is per-sprint; pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at `0` until go-live, which becomes `v1.0.0`); `Test` gets its own automated CI gate (not manual-only); tag protection + the version-guard + Release-per-final-tag are all adopted immediately, not phased in.
  - **Tooling — safe to build now, doesn't touch governance docs:**
    1. `npm version` adoption — no code change needed, it's a built-in npm command; just start using it per the Confluence page's "How to deploy" section instead of raw `git tag`. First tag will be `v0.1.0-rc.0`.
    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.
    5. Wire `/generate-changelog`'s existing `gh release create` offer into the "cut the final tag" step — no new tooling, the skill already does this.
  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**
    6. A new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or fold into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`) documenting the tag convention and instructing Claude to always use `npm version`, never hand-construct a tag string.
    7. `AGENTS.md`'s branch table / the Confluence Branching Guide itself, once the team has actually reviewed and approved the proposal — this repo's `AGENTS.md` requires both squad leads and the Integration lead to sign off on changes to itself, stronger than the usual verified-session Tier 1 exception.
